# Pylon — full operational manual

> This is the inline reference an agent reads to BUILD a Pylon app without leaving the file. Every API name, signature, env var, and CLI flag below is taken from source. Code snippets are minimal and copy-paste-correct. The short curated index lives at /llms.txt.

Pylon is a Rails-like framework for realtime apps. You declare entities, policies, and server functions in TypeScript; a single Rust binary (`pylon`) serves the API, auth, sync, WebSocket, SSE, and a native React 19 server-rendered frontend — all from one process and one port. Storage is SQLite by default or Postgres via `DATABASE_URL`; the app model is identical across both.

The four core primitives:
- **Entities** — typed tables (`entity()` + `field.*`).
- **Policies** — row-level access rules, CEL-like expressions over `auth.*` / `data.*`, deny-by-default.
- **Functions** — `query()` / `mutation()` / `action()` in TypeScript, RPC-called by the client; secure-by-default (`auth: "user"`).
- **Live queries** — client subscriptions that restream when dependent rows change.

> Server functions BYPASS policies (they run with full DB access). HTTP entity CRUD (`/api/entities/*`) and client sync ARE policy-checked. Put trust boundaries in policies for direct client access, and in `ctx.auth` checks inside functions.

---

# 1. Getting started & scaffolding

Scaffold with `@pylonsync/create-pylon` (a zero-dependency Node script; works with any package manager's `create` runner, no Bun required):

```bash
npm create @pylonsync/pylon@latest [name] --template <t>
```

Flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--template <t>` | `ssr` \| `barebones` \| `todo` \| `b2b` \| `consumer` \| `chat` (interactive default: `todo`) |
| `--platforms <list>` | comma list from `web,vite,ios,mac,expo` (default `web`). Ignored for `ssr`. |
| `--bun` / `--pnpm` / `--yarn` / `--npm` | package manager (auto-detected; falls back to `bun`) |
| `--skip-install` | scaffold only |
| `--help`, `-h` | usage |

Templates:

| `--template` | What it is | Platforms |
|---|---|---|
| `ssr` | Full-stack SSR — server-rendered React + Link/Image/Tailwind, one server, no Next.js | *(unified single app)* |
| `barebones` | Single entity, list + create. Smallest working app. | web, ios, mac, expo |
| `todo` | CRUD + drag-reorder + optimistic mutations | web, vite, ios, mac, expo |
| `b2b` | Multi-tenant SaaS: orgs, members, roles, RBAC | web, mac |
| `consumer` | Social feed: profiles, posts, likes, follows | web, ios, mac, expo |
| `chat` | Realtime messaging: rooms, presence, live feed | web, ios, mac, expo |

Examples:

```bash
npm create @pylonsync/pylon my-app --template ssr            # full-stack SSR, no Next.js
npm create @pylonsync/pylon my-app --template todo --platforms web,ios
npm create @pylonsync/pylon my-app --template b2b --platforms web,mac
npm create @pylonsync/pylon my-app --template chat --platforms ios,mac,expo
```

First run:

```bash
npm create @pylonsync/pylon my-app --template ssr
cd my-app
npm run dev            # pm-aware; pylon dev serves SSR + API on :4321
# open http://localhost:4321
```

## Directory conventions

**Unified SSR (`--template ssr`):**

```
app.ts            data model + manifest (entities, queries, actions, policies, routes)
app/              file-based SSR routes — app/page.tsx → "/", app/counter/page.tsx → "/counter"
app/layout.tsx    root layout wrapping every page
app/globals.css   Tailwind entrypoint (compiled by Pylon; stylesheet auto-injected)
functions/        server functions (query/mutation/action) — typed RPC, auto-discovered
.pylon/           local dev state (sqlite, jobs, sessions, uploads) — created by pylon dev
```

`app.ts` ends with `buildManifest({ ..., routes: await discoverAppRoutes() })` and `console.log(JSON.stringify(manifest))`. Scripts: `dev: pylon dev`, `deploy: pylon deploy`, `check: tsc --noEmit`. Deps: `@pylonsync/react`, `@pylonsync/sdk`, `@pylonsync/functions`; devDep `@pylonsync/cli`.

**Monorepo (all other templates):**

```
apps/api/         Pylon backend — schema.ts, functions/, policies
apps/web/         Next.js 16 (or Vite) frontend          (if web/vite picked)
apps/ios/         Swift / SwiftUI iOS                     (if ios picked)
apps/mac/         Swift / SwiftUI macOS                   (if mac picked)
apps/expo/        Expo + React Native                     (if expo picked)
packages/ui/      shared shadcn-style React primitives    (web/vite only)
.pylon/           local dev state
```

Backend entry is `apps/api/schema.ts` (not `app.ts`). It ends with `console.log(JSON.stringify(manifest))`; `pylon dev` / `pylon codegen` run the entry file and read the manifest off stdout, emitting `pylon.manifest.json` + `pylon.client.ts`. Handlers live in `apps/api/functions/<name>.ts`, auto-discovered by filename.

---

# 2. Schema DSL — `@pylonsync/sdk`

The schema layer compiles entity/field/policy/route declarations into an `AppManifest` (JSON) the Rust runtime consumes. Two equivalent surfaces: the procedural API (`entity()` + `field.*` + `policy({...})`) and the fluent `e` namespace. Both compile to the same shapes and can be mixed.

## `entity()`

```ts
function entity(
  name: string,
  fields: Record<string, FieldBuilder>,
  options?: {
    indexes?: IndexDefinition[];
    relations?: RelationDefinition[];
    search?: SearchConfig;
  },
): EntityDefinition
```

## Field types — `field.*`

| Builder | Type emitted | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `field.string()` | `"string"` | |
| `field.int()` | `"int"` | |
| `field.float()` / `field.number()` | `"float"` | aliases |
| `field.bool()` / `field.boolean()` | `"bool"` | aliases |
| `field.datetime()` | `"datetime"` | |
| `field.richtext()` | `"richtext"` | LoroText CRDT by default |
| `field.id(target)` | `id(<target>)` | FK reference, e.g. `field.id("User")` |
| `field.enum(values)` | `"string"` | records `enumValues` for codegen literal-union typing |

## Field modifiers (chainable)

| Modifier | Effect |
|---|---|
| `.optional()` | field may be omitted / null |
| `.unique()` | uniqueness constraint — cannot combine with `.encrypted()` |
| `.crdt(annotation)` | override CRDT container (below) |
| `.serverOnly()` | never serialized in HTTP responses; still readable via `ctx.db.*` server-side |
| `.readonly()` | settable on insert, rejected on client PATCH/PUT with `READONLY_FIELD`; admin + server writes bypass |
| `.encrypted()` | AEAD-encrypted at rest (ChaCha20-Poly1305, key `PYLON_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) |
| `.default(value)` | default literal on insert |
| `.defaultNow()` | stamp current UTC time on insert |

`.serverOnly()` strips the field at every public read boundary: entity list/single GETs, `GET /api/auth/session` (User projection), and sync push deltas. `passwordHash` on a User entity is implicitly serverOnly by framework convention; marking it explicitly is still recommended.

`.readonly()` is rejected before policy evaluation with `READONLY_FIELD` on `PATCH /api/entities/<entity>/<id>` and `/api/transact`. Use for `authorId`, `orgId`, `createdBy`, `stripeCustomerId` — closes the IDOR-via-update-payload class.

`.encrypted()` (ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, on-disk `enc:v1:<base64nonce>:<base64ciphertext>`): NOT queryable (fresh ciphertext per write, so `WHERE encryptedField = 'x'` returns nothing); cannot combine with `.unique()`; valid only on `string`, `richtext`, and JSON-shaped fields. Rows written before the annotation read back as plaintext and upgrade to ciphertext on the next mutation. Requires `PYLON_ENCRYPTION_KEY` or boot fails.

CRDT annotations (`.crdt(annotation)`): `"lww"` (explicit last-write-wins, the default for scalars), `"text"` (upgrade a `string` to LoroText character-level merge), `"counter"` (flip `int`/`float` to LoroCounter — concurrent increments add), `"list"` / `"movable-list"` / `"tree"` (wire format locked; server projection pending). Default when omitted: `string`→LWW, `richtext`→LoroText.

## Composite & partial indexes

```ts
interface IndexDefinition {
  name: string;
  fields: string[];   // multiple field names → composite index
  unique: boolean;
  where?: string;     // partial-index SQL predicate — NOT validated/escaped; never interpolate user input
}
```

Pass via `entity(..., { indexes: [...] })`. Fluent helper: `e.idx("customer", "createdAt")`.

## `policy()`

```ts
interface PolicyDefinition {
  name?: string;        // auto-generated if omitted
  entity?: string;
  action?: string;
  allow?: string;        // single-gate fallback
  allowRead?: string;    // reads (pull, list, get)
  allowInsert?: string;  // inserts; falls back to allowWrite
  allowUpdate?: string;  // updates; falls back to allowWrite/allow
  allowDelete?: string;  // deletes; falls back to allowWrite/allow
  allowWrite?: string;   // shared fallback for any write
}
```

Each rule is a CEL-like expression string over `auth` / `data` (e.g. `"auth.userId == data.authorId || auth.hasRole('admin')"`). Gate resolution: `allowRead` for reads; `allowInsert` for inserts (→ `allowWrite`); `allowUpdate`/`allowDelete` override `allow`/`allowWrite`; `allow` is the single-gate fallback. **An action with no matching gate is denied.** Set `entity` to gate a table's rows; `action` to gate a named action. The fluent `.policies(...)` chain auto-binds `entity` and auto-generates a `name`.

## Routes

```ts
function defineRoute(route: RouteDefinition): RouteDefinition

type RouteMode = "static" | "server" | "live" | "ssr";
type AuthMode  = "public" | "user";

interface RouteDefinition {
  path: string;
  mode: RouteMode;
  query?: string;
  auth?: AuthMode;
  component?: string;            // required when mode === "ssr"
  layouts?: string[];            // layout chain root→leaf; SSR only
  kind?: "page" | "not-found" | "error";
}
```

`discoverAppRoutes(opts?: { appDir?: string }): Promise<RouteDefinition[]>` walks `app/` (default `<cwd>/app`) and returns routes ready for `buildManifest({ routes })`. Node-only (returns `[]` in a browser bundle). Mapping is Next App Router-shaped:

- `app/page.tsx` → `/`
- `app/about/page.tsx` → `/about`
- `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` → `/blog/:slug`
- `app/layout.tsx` wraps every page below (chain accumulated root→leaf)
- `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx` → `/about` (route group `(...)` stripped)
- `not-found.tsx` / `error.tsx` → boundary routes (`kind` set), NOT navigable URLs

## `buildManifest()`

```ts
function buildManifest(options: {
  name: string;
  version: string;
  entities: EntityDefinition[];
  routes: RouteDefinition[];
  queries?: QueryDefinition[];
  actions?: ActionDefinition[];
  policies?: PolicyDefinition[];
  auth?: ManifestAuthConfig;
  llm?: ManifestLlmConfig;
  connections?: ManifestConnection[];
}): AppManifest
```

Assembles the `AppManifest` (`manifest_version: 1`). Pulls policies attached via the fluent `.policies(...)` chain onto the top-level list (explicit top-level beats attached). `auth` defaults to `auth()` when omitted; `llm`/`connections` emitted only when non-empty.

## Minimal correct schema

```ts
import { entity, field, policy, defineRoute, buildManifest } from "@pylonsync/sdk";

const User = entity("User", {
  email:        field.string().unique(),
  displayName:  field.string(),
  passwordHash: field.string().serverOnly(),
});

const Post = entity(
  "Post",
  {
    authorId:  field.id("User").readonly(),
    title:     field.string(),
    body:      field.richtext(),          // collaborative LoroText by default
    published: field.bool(),
  },
  { indexes: [{ name: "by_author_published", fields: ["authorId", "published"], unique: false }] },
);

export default buildManifest({
  name: "blog",
  version: "0.1.0",
  entities: [User, Post],
  routes: [defineRoute({ path: "/api/posts", mode: "live", auth: "user" })],
  policies: [
    policy({
      entity: "Post",
      allowRead:   "data.published == true || auth.userId == data.authorId",
      allowInsert: "auth.userId == data.authorId",
      allowUpdate: "auth.userId == data.authorId",
      allowDelete: "auth.userId == data.authorId",
    }),
  ],
});
```

---

# 3. Functions — `@pylonsync/functions`

```ts
import { query, mutation, action, v } from "@pylonsync/functions";
```

Three constructors take one definition object and return an `FnDefinition`. Export the result as the module's `default`.

## Shared definition fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `args?` | `Record<string, Validator>` | arg name → `v.*` validator. Validated before the handler; drives arg type inference. |
| `handler` | `(ctx, args) => Promise<TReturn>` | function body. `ctx` type depends on the constructor. |
| `auth?` | `"public" \| "guest" \| "user" \| "admin"` | enforced before the handler. Defaults to `"user"`. |
| `internal?` | `boolean` | when `true`, callable only via `ctx.runQuery/runMutation`; public `/api/fn/<name>` returns `404 FN_NOT_FOUND`. |

`auth` (default `"user"` — secure-by-default): `"public"` (anyone, must be explicit), `"guest"` (anonymous-with-stable-id + any user), `"user"` (real signed-in user; `ctx.auth.userId` narrows to `string`), `"admin"` (`ctx.auth.isAdmin === true`). Under `"public"`/`"guest"`, `ctx.auth.userId` is `string | null`.

## The three constructors

- **`query(def)`** — read-only, runs on the read pool, concurrent, cannot write. Receives `QueryCtx`. **No `ctx.llm`** (reactive purity).
- **`mutation(def)`** — transactional read + write. The handler IS the transaction: return → all writes (and scheduled functions) commit atomically; throw → all roll back. Receives `MutationCtx`. Can stream via `ctx.stream`.
- **`action(def)`** — external I/O allowed (fetch, email, Stripe). **No direct `ctx.db`** — use `ctx.runQuery` / `ctx.runMutation` (each its own transaction). Not auto-retried. Policies don't gate actions — `auth` is the only protection. Receives `ActionCtx`.

## Validators (`v.*`)

| Validator | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `v.string()` | string | |
| `v.number()` / `v.float()` | number (float64) | aliases; prefer `v.float()` in new code |
| `v.int()` | number (`int`) | |
| `v.boolean()` / `v.bool()` | boolean | aliases; prefer `v.bool()` |
| `v.datetime()` | string | ISO-8601 datetime |
| `v.richtext()` | string | same validation as `v.string()`, named for readability |
| `v.id(table)` | string | ID reference; sets `table` |
| `v.null()` | null | |
| `v.array(items)` | array | validates each element |
| `v.object(fields)` | object | typed nested fields; honors per-field `optional` |
| `v.optional(inner)` | inner-or-omitted | |
| `v.union(...variants)` | one of | |
| `v.literal(value)` | exact literal | `string \| number \| boolean` |
| `v.any()` | any JSON | no validation |

## Handler context (`ctx`)

**`QueryCtx`:** `ctx.db` (`DbReader`, read-only), `ctx.auth`, `ctx.env`. No stream/scheduler/llm/connections/runQuery.

**`MutationCtx`:** `ctx.db` (`DbWriter`, read + write), `ctx.auth`, `ctx.stream`, `ctx.scheduler`, `ctx.env`, `ctx.llm`, `ctx.connections`, `ctx.error(code, message)`. No runQuery/email/request.

**`ActionCtx`:** `ctx.auth`, `ctx.stream`, `ctx.scheduler`, `ctx.email`, `ctx.llm`, `ctx.connections`, `ctx.env`, `ctx.runQuery<T>(fnName, args)`, `ctx.runMutation<T>(fnName, args)`, `ctx.error(code, message)`, `ctx.request?`. **No direct `ctx.db`.** `ctx.request` (`{ method, path, headers, rawBody }`, headers lowercased) is present only when invoked via a `defineRoute` HTTP binding.

### `ctx.auth` — `AuthInfo`

`userId` (`string` under `auth:"user"`/`"admin"`, else `string | null`), `isAdmin: boolean`, `tenantId: string | null` (active selected org), `elevate({ admin: boolean; reason: string }): Promise<void>` (promote after a custom check e.g. webhook HMAC; `reason` mandatory, logged at INFO; mutates `auth.isAdmin` locally).

### `ctx.db` — `DbReader` / `DbWriter`

Read (everywhere `db` exists): `get(entity, id)`, `list(entity)`, `lookup(entity, field, value)`, `query(entity, filter)` (filter supports `$gt`/`$lt`/`$in`/`$like`/`$order`/`$limit`), `queryGraph(query)` (nested relation includes), `search(entity, query)` → `SearchResult` (throws `SEARCH_NOT_CONFIGURED` without a `search:` config), `paginate(entity, { cursor, numItems })` → `{ page, nextCursor, isDone }` (`numItems` clamped to `[1, 1000]`), and `unsafe?` (policy-bypass escape hatch).

Write (mutation `ctx.db` only; `DbWriter` extends `DbReader`): `insert(entity, data)` → `string` (id), `update(entity, id, data)` → `boolean`, `delete(entity, id)` → `boolean`, `link(entity, id, relation, targetId)`, `unlink(entity, id, relation)`, `advisoryLock(key)` (tx-scoped; serializes concurrent mutations on Postgres, noop on SQLite — call before count/uniqueness checks to close TOCTOU windows).

### `ctx.scheduler` — `Scheduler` (mutation + action)

`runAfter(delayMs, fnName, args)` → scheduleId, `runAt(timestamp, fnName, args)` → scheduleId (Unix ms), `cancel(scheduleId)`. **This is the deferred/jobs surface — there is no separate `jobs` or `workflows` primitive.** Scheduled functions from a mutation roll back with the transaction.

### `ctx.stream` — `Stream` (mutation + action)

`write(data: string)` (text chunk over SSE), `writeEvent(event: string, data: string)` (typed SSE event).

### `ctx.error(code, message)`

Returns a typed `Error`. Throwing it in a mutation triggers rollback.

## Minimal example — mutation + query

```ts
import { mutation, query, v } from "@pylonsync/functions";

export const placeBid = mutation({
  args: { lotId: v.id("Lot"), amount: v.number() },
  async handler(ctx, args) {
    const lot = await ctx.db.get("Lot", args.lotId);
    if (!lot) throw ctx.error("NOT_FOUND", "Lot not found");
    const bidId = await ctx.db.insert("Bid", {
      lotId: args.lotId,
      amount: args.amount,
      bidderId: ctx.auth.userId,   // non-null under default auth: "user"
    });
    return { bidId };
  },
});

export const listBids = query({
  args: { lotId: v.id("Lot") },
  async handler(ctx, args) {
    return ctx.db.query("Bid", { lotId: args.lotId, $order: "amount" });
  },
});
```

---

# 4. Server primitives (`ctx.*`)

Each primitive's TS surface round-trips through the Rust host runtime, which owns provider config and credentials so secrets never leave the server process.

## `ctx.llm` — provider-abstracted LLM completion (mutation + action; NOT query)

```ts
complete(request: LlmCompleteRequest): Promise<LlmCompleteResponse>;

interface LlmCompleteRequest {
  model?: string;          // gated by PYLON_AI_MODELS_ALLOWED for non-admin callers
  messages: LlmMessage[];  // { role: "user"|"assistant"|"system"|"tool", content: string | LlmContentBlock[] }
  system?: string;
  tools?: LlmTool[];       // { name, description?, input_schema: JSON Schema object }
  max_tokens?: number;     // default 4096
  temperature?: number;
}
interface LlmCompleteResponse {
  model: string;
  content: LlmContentBlock[];  // union of {type:"text"} | {type:"tool_use",id,name,input} | {type:"tool_result",...}
  stop_reason: string;          // "end_turn" | "tool_use" | "max_tokens" | "stop_sequence"
  usage: { input_tokens: number; output_tokens: number };
}
```

Wire shape is Anthropic Messages; OpenAI calls are translated at the transport boundary. Server-only — the key never reaches the browser (browser streaming uses `POST /api/ai/stream`). Errors thrown with `err.code` ∈ `LLM_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED`, `MODEL_OVERRIDE_FORBIDDEN`, `PROVIDER_HTTP_<code>`, `PROVIDER_UNREACHABLE`, `INVALID_REQUEST`. For agent loops, branch on `stop_reason === "tool_use"`, append assistant content + your `tool_result` blocks, and call again until `end_turn`.

```ts
const res = await ctx.llm.complete({
  system: "You are concise.",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Summarize this in one line: ..." }],
  max_tokens: 256,
});
const text = res.content.find(b => b.type === "text")?.text;
```

Config: `PYLON_LLM_PROVIDER` = `anthropic` | `openai` (auto-detected from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`); `PYLON_LLM_MODEL` pins the default (else `claude-sonnet-4-5` / `gpt-4o-mini`); `PYLON_AI_MODELS_ALLOWED` gates client-supplied `model` overrides for non-admins. Manifest-level via the `llm({ provider?, defaultModel?, allowedModels? })` factory; env wins over manifest.

## `ctx.connections` — per-user OAuth integrations (mutation + action; NOT query)

```ts
authorizeUrl(name, opts?: { postRedirect?: string }): Promise<{ url: string }>;
get(name): Promise<{ accessToken: string; scope: string | null; expiresAt: number | null }>;  // auto-refreshes if expiring within 60s
list(): Promise<{ connections: Array<{ name; provider; scope; expiresAt; updatedAt }> }>;       // no token values
disconnect(name): Promise<{ disconnected: boolean }>;
```

Declare connections in the manifest and `ctx.connections.get(name)` matches on the connection `name`. Tokens stored AEAD-encrypted in an auto-created `_Connection` entity. All ops require an authenticated caller; public functions must `ctx.auth.elevate({ admin: true, reason: "..." })` first. Throws: `CONNECTIONS_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `CONNECTION_UNKNOWN`, `PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `ENCRYPTION_REQUIRED`, `CONNECTION_NOT_LINKED`, `REFRESH_FAILED`.

```ts
import { defineConnection } from "@pylonsync/sdk";

export const googleConn = defineConnection({
  name: "google",          // app-facing key; ctx.connections.get("google") matches this
  provider: "google",      // matches the OAuth client list (google, github, slack, microsoft, ...)
  scopes: "email profile https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly",
});
// → buildManifest({ connections: [googleConn] })
```

```ts
const { url } = await ctx.connections.authorizeUrl("google", { postRedirect: "/settings" });
// later, in an action:
const { accessToken } = await ctx.connections.get("google");
await fetch("https://www.googleapis.com/...", { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` } });
```

Config: `PYLON_OAUTH_<PROVIDER>_CLIENT_ID` / `_CLIENT_SECRET` (optional `_REDIRECT`, `_OIDC_ISSUER`). Callback derived from `PYLON_PUBLIC_URL` (or `PYLON_CONNECTIONS_CALLBACK_BASE`) + `/api/connections/<name>/callback`. `PYLON_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is REQUIRED when any connection is declared.

## `ctx.email` — transactional email (action only)

`send(to: string, subject: string, body: string): Promise<void>` via the configured `PYLON_EMAIL_PROVIDER` (`sendgrid` | `resend` | `stack0` | `webhook`; SMTP supported).

## Search (`ctx.db.search`) — full-text / faceted

Search is a method on the DB reader (available wherever `ctx.db` exists), not a top-level primitive:

```ts
search(entity: string, query: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<SearchResult>;

interface SearchResult<T = Record<string, unknown>> {
  hits: T[];
  facetCounts: Record<string, Record<string, number>>;  // {facet: {value: count}}
  total: number;     // total hits before pagination
  tookMs: number;
}
```

```ts
const result = await ctx.db.search("Product", {
  query: "rust async",
  filters: { brand: "Atlas" },
  facets: ["category"],
  page: 0,
  pageSize: 20,
});
```

Throws `SEARCH_NOT_CONFIGURED` on entities without a `search:` config (set via `entity(..., { search: {...} })`).

## `field.encrypted()` — AEAD encryption at rest

```ts
apiKey: field.string().serverOnly().encrypted(),
```

ChaCha20-Poly1305 (`ring`), 96-bit per-cell nonce, on-disk `enc:v1:<base64nonce>:<base64ciphertext>`. Requires `PYLON_ENCRYPTION_KEY` — a 32-byte key as 64-char hex (`openssl rand -hex 32`) or base64 — or boot fails when encrypted fields/connections are declared. `serverOnly()` (out of HTTP responses) and `encrypted()` (encrypted bytes at rest) compose.

> There is NO `ctx.files` server primitive. File handling is via the `<FileUpload>` client component + the `/api/files/*` endpoints + provider config (`PYLON_FILES_PROVIDER`). Likewise there is no `defineWorkflow`/`defineJob` — deferred execution is `ctx.scheduler`.

---

# 5. Client — `@pylonsync/react`

Client-side hooks/components for talking to a Pylon backend. Use from client components in an SSR app, or any React / React-Native app. Configure once with `init()`, then read/write via `db` + hooks.

## Setup

```ts
import { init } from "@pylonsync/react";

// Call once at startup. In a browser, omitting baseUrl falls back to
// window.location.origin (right for same-origin deploys) — NOT localhost.
init({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:4321", appName: "myapp" });
```

- `init(config?)` — creates the global sync engine; `config.appName` namespaces all client storage.
- `configureClient({ baseUrl?, appName? })` — config the free helpers (`callFn`, session) without a sync engine.
- `storageKey(slot)` — resolves a slot (`"token"`, `"user"`) to its localStorage key. Related: `getBaseUrl()`, `getAppName()`, `setReactStorage()`, `getReactStorage()`.

## Data hooks (`db`)

`db` is the untyped one-liner API:

```tsx
const { data, loading, error } = db.useQuery<Todo>("Todo", { where: { done: false } });
const { data: todo, loading } = db.useQueryOne<Todo>("Todo", "todo_1");   // single row by id (NOT useOne)
```

Other `db` members: `useReactiveQuery(fnName, args?)`, `useMutation(fnName, { optimistic? })`, `useInfiniteQuery(entity, { pageSize? })`, `useAggregate(entity, spec)`, `useSearch(entity, spec)`, `useEntity(entity)`, `db.sync`, `insert/update/delete`, `setPresence`, `publishTopic`, `fn(name, args?)`, `streamFn(name, args?)`, `uploadFile`, `uploadFileMultipart`.

Top-level hook exports (take an explicit `SyncEngine` as first arg; `db.*` pre-supplies the global one): `useQuery`, `useQueryOne`, `useReactiveQuery`, `useMutation`, `useInfiniteQuery`, `usePaginatedQuery`, `useEntityMutation`, `useAction`, `useQueryRaw`, `useQueryOneRaw`, `useLiveList`, `useLiveRow`, `useInsert`, `useUpdate`, `useDelete`, `useFn`, `useAggregate`, `useSearch`.

## Server function calls

```ts
const result = await callFn("placeBid", { lotId: "lot_1", amount: 150 });       // POST /api/fn/<name>
for await (const chunk of streamFn("chat", { message: "hello" })) console.log(chunk);  // SSE
```

`callFn<T>(name, args?, { token? })` and `streamFn(name, args?, { token? })` are free helpers (token read from storage). Inside synced apps, prefer `db.fn(...)` (honors the change-seq fallback pull); `db.streamFn` delegates to the free `streamFn`.

## Session & realtime

```tsx
const { userId, isAuthenticated, selectOrg, signOut } = useSession(db.sync);
const status = useSyncStatus();   // "connecting" | "connected" | "reconnecting" | "offline"; SSR snapshot "offline"
```

`useSession(sync)` returns `session`, `userId`, `tenantId`, `isAdmin`, `isAuthenticated`, `selectOrg(orgId)`, `clearOrg()`, `signOut()`, `refresh()`. Watches the localStorage token for cross-tab sign-in/out.

```tsx
const { peers, isConnected, setPresence, broadcast, leave, error } =
  useRoom("project-42", currentUser.id, { token });   // presence room; WS push, 5s poll fallback
const { snapshot, tick, send, connected, error, close } =
  useShard("match1", { subscriberId: "player42", token });   // sharded sims; WS-preferred, SSE fallback
```

## Navigation & images

```tsx
<Link href="/dashboard" prefetch>Dashboard</Link>   // SSR-safe; renders plain <a>, client intercepts + prefetches
<Image src="/hero.jpg" width={1200} height={630} alt="Hero" priority />  // Rust optimizer /_pylon/image
```

`<Link>`: same-origin paths get client nav; off-origin / `#` / `mailto:` / `tel:` / modifier-click / `target="_blank"` fall through to native. `<Image>` props: `src`, `width`, `height`, `alt` (required), `quality?` (1..100, default 75), `widths?`, `sizes?` (default `"100vw"`), `priority?`, `unoptimized?`. Server emits WebP/JPEG/PNG (no AVIF), no blur placeholder; remote hosts must be in `PYLON_IMAGE_REMOTE_ALLOWLIST`.

## Typed client

```ts
import { createTypedDb } from "@pylonsync/react";
import type { AppSchema } from "./pylon.client";   // from `pylon codegen client`
export const db = createTypedDb<AppSchema>();

const { data } = db.useQuery("Todo");                 // data: Todo[]
const { data: user } = db.useQueryOne("User", "u_1"); // user: User | null
const bid = db.useMutation("placeBid");               // typed args + result
```

`TypedDb<S>` exposes `useQuery`, `useQueryOne`, `useMutation`, `useInfiniteQuery`, `fn`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`, and `untyped` (escape hatch). Same object as `db` at runtime; narrowed at compile time.

---

# 6. Client components — `@pylonsync/client`

Clerk-style drop-in component library. Every component is a Client Component, renders nothing for signed-out users where auth is required, and is a UX convenience only — server-side policy enforcement is the source of truth. Auth comes from `useAuth()` (wraps `useSession(db.sync)`); no provider required as long as the app has `init()`-ed the global engine. Theming via CSS variables (import `@pylonsync/client/theme.css` or set the `--pylon-*` tokens); every component takes a `className`.

**Auth:** `<SignIn method?="magic"|"password" />`, `<SignUp />`, `<ForgotPassword />`, `<ResetPassword />`, `<UserButton />`, `<UserProfile />`, `<SignOutButton />`, `<EnsureGuest />` (mints a guest session for zero-auth demos).

**Render gates:** `<SignedIn>`, `<SignedOut>`, `<Protect admin? predicate?>`, `<HasRole role mode?="any"|"all">`, `<InOrg>`, `<NoOrg>`, `<RedirectToSignIn signInUrl?="/sign-in" />`.

**Orgs:** `<OrganizationSwitcher />`, `<CreateOrganization />`, `<InviteMembers orgId? roles?=["member","admin"] />`, `<AcceptInvite />`.

**Integration:** `<ConnectAccount name="google" />` (`name` is the connection name from `defineConnection`, NOT the OAuth provider id), `<FileUpload onUploaded? accept? multiple? maxSizeBytes? />`, `<ChatBot fn="..." />` (streams via `db.streamFn(fn, { messages })`).

**Data:** `<EntityList entity columns? where? orderBy? limit? onRowClick? />` (wraps `db.useQuery`, live), `<EntityForm entity fields row? />` (create/edit via `db.useEntity` optimistic CRUD).

**Router (optional SPA):** `<Router routes notFound? />`, `<Outlet />`, `<Link href replace? />`, hooks `useRouter()`, `useParams()`, `useSearchParams()`, `usePathname()`. `RouteSpec = { path; component?; element?; requireAuth?: boolean|"admin"; signInUrl?; children? }`; patterns support `:param`, `:param?`, `/*`.

**`useAuth()`** returns `{ isSignedIn, isLoaded, userId, tenantId, isAdmin, session, signOut, selectOrg, clearOrg, refresh }`.

Low-level API helpers (same endpoints the components use, for custom auth surfaces): `passwordLogin`, `passwordRegister`, `sendMagicLink`, `verifyMagicLink`, `requestPasswordReset`, `completePasswordReset`, `changePassword`, `createOrg`, `listOrgs`, `createInvite`, `acceptInvite`, `listOrgMembers`, `updateMemberRole`, `removeMember`, `createApiKey`, `listApiKeys`, `revokeApiKey`, `listActiveSessions`, `revokeAllSessions`, `ensureGuestSession`, `connectionAuthUrl`, `listAuthProviders`, and more.

---

# 7. Native SSR

Pylon serves React 19 server-rendered pages from the same binary and port as the API. Pages live under `app/`, render via `react-dom/server.renderToReadableStream`, and hydrate into an interactive SPA with client-side navigation. No `web/dist` build required — an app with SSR routes IS a frontend app; per-route client chunks build lazily on first request.

```bash
npm create @pylonsync/pylon --template ssr
```

## File routing

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `app/page.tsx` | `/` route (component is the `default` export; also accepts named `Page`/`page`) |
| `app/hello/page.tsx` | `/hello` — directory names become URL segments |
| `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` | dynamic segment → `params.slug` |
| `app/(marketing)/page.tsx` | route group — `(…)` stripped from the URL |
| `app/layout.tsx` | layout, wraps every page at/below its directory |

Extensions tried in order: `.tsx`, `.ts`, `.jsx`, `.js`.

### Layout chains

Layouts nest root→leaf. For `app/blog/[slug]/page` with layouts `[app/layout, app/blog/layout]`:

```
<RootLayout><BlogLayout><Page {...props} /></BlogLayout></RootLayout>
```

Each layout's `default` (or named `Layout`/`layout`) receives the page props plus `children`. The root layout typically renders the `<html>`/`<head>`/`<body>` shell.

## Boundaries — `error.tsx` + `not-found.tsx`

Place anywhere in `app/`. At render time the framework walks UP to the nearest boundary, then renders it inside the route's layout chain. Boundaries render server-side only (no hydration) but get the global stylesheet injected.

- **`not-found.tsx`** (HTTP **404**) triggers on `response.notFound()` or an unmatched document-navigation URL (no file extension in the last segment); nearest-by-longest-prefix wins. If none exists, a built-in 404 is served.
- **`error.tsx`** (HTTP **500**) triggers when a page/layout throws during the synchronous shell render; the error is passed as `props.error` (`error.message`). If none exists, a host-level 500 is served.

```tsx
// app/error.tsx
interface ErrorProps { error?: { message?: string } }
export default function ErrorBoundary({ error }: ErrorProps) {
  return <div>500 — {error?.message ?? "unknown error"}</div>;
}
```

## Metadata

```tsx
export const metadata = { title: "Hello", description: "..." };
// or, param-derived (await-ed before the first byte; takes precedence over static metadata):
export async function generateMetadata(props) {
  return { title: `Post ${props.params.slug}` };
}
```

`SsrMetadata` fields (all optional): `title`, `description`, `keywords` (`string | string[]`), `canonical`, `robots`, `openGraph` (`{ title?, description?, image?, url?, type? }`), `twitter` (`{ card?, title?, description?, image? }`). React 19 auto-hoists these into `<head>`; a page `title` overrides a layout `<title>`. React does NOT dedupe arbitrary `<meta>` — set `description`/OG in EITHER the layout OR the page, not both.

## Page props

Every page and layout receives one props object:

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | incoming URL path |
| `params` | `Record<string,string>` | dynamic-segment matches |
| `searchParams` | `Record<string,string>` | parsed query string |
| `headers` | `Record<string,string>` | lowercased names |
| `cookies` | `Record<string,string>` | parsed request cookies |
| `auth` | `{ user_id, is_admin, tenant_id, roles }` | resolved from the session cookie; anonymous (`user_id: null`) when none |
| `response` | `SsrResponse` | per-render response controller |
| `serverData` | read-only `DbReader` | server-side data handle |

Layouts additionally receive `children`.

## serverData (READ-ONLY)

`serverData` is a read-only `DbReader` reached during render via React 19 `use()` inside `<Suspense>`. Runs against the same store + policy gate as a query's `ctx.db`.

```tsx
import { Suspense, use } from "react";

function MarkerList({ serverData }) {
  const markers = use(serverData.list("Marker"));
  return <>{markers.map((m) => <li key={m.id}>{m.note}</li>)}</>;
}

export default function DataPage({ serverData }) {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<li>Loading…</li>}>
      <MarkerList serverData={serverData} />
    </Suspense>
  );
}
```

Methods: `get`, `list`, `lookup`, `query`, `queryGraph`, `paginate`, `search` (+ `serverData.unsafe.*`). Each call returns a promise cached by `(method, args)`, so `use()` re-reads resolve instead of re-suspending. Resolved values are serialized into the hydration payload (`__PYLON_DATA__.ssrData`) — the client hydrates from the SSR'd data with no refetch and no mismatch (the server waits for `stream.allReady` before emitting the body).

> **GOTCHA #1 — serverData is READ-ONLY.** No write methods exist; the Rust render loop rejects any write frame (`SSR_WRITE_FORBIDDEN`). Mutations belong in actions/functions, not in a page render.

## Response controller

| Method | Effect |
|---|---|
| `response.setStatus(code)` | set status; integer `100`–`599` (else throws); default `200` |
| `response.setHeader(name, value)` | set a header; `name` an RFC token, `value` CR/LF/NUL-free (injection-safe) |
| `response.setCookie(name, value, opts?)` | append `Set-Cookie`; defaults `HttpOnly` + `SameSite=Lax`. opts: `path` (`/`), `domain`, `maxAge`, `expires`, `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite` |
| `response.redirect(url, status?)` | **throws** to send a `3xx` (default `307`) + `Location`, no body |
| `response.notFound()` | **throws** to send `404`, rendering the nearest `not-found.tsx` |

```tsx
export default function Page({ auth, response }) {
  if (!auth.user_id) response.redirect("/login");      // 307 + Location
  response.setStatus(201);
  response.setCookie("seen", "1", { maxAge: 3600 });
  return <h1>OK</h1>;
}
```

> **GOTCHA #2 — `response.*` / `redirect` / `notFound` must fire in the synchronous shell render**, before any `await` / `<Suspense>` boundary. The HTTP head is committed when the shell is ready, so status/headers/cookies set from a suspended subtree that streams in later are LOST. A `redirect()` / `notFound()` thrown below a Suspense boundary is caught by React's error handling instead of becoming a 3xx/404 — and an enclosing `error.tsx` would swallow the control signal. Throw these from the top-level component body, outside any boundary.

## Styling

If `app/globals.css` exists, the bundler compiles it through Tailwind v4 (`@tailwindcss/cli` + `tailwindcss` must be installed) and injects the hashed `<link rel="stylesheet">` into every route's `<head>`. Without `app/globals.css`, the Tailwind step is skipped silently.

---

# 8. Runtime, endpoints & environment

## The `pylon` binary

One Rust binary serves API, auth, sync, static/SSR frontend, WebSocket, and SSE from one process. Two run modes:

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `pylon dev [app.ts] [--port N] [--once]` | Dev server. Auto-creates `.pylon/`, sets `PYLON_DEV_MODE=1` if unset, watches `*.ts` for hot rebuilds, serves the frontend behind the one port. `--once` validates/builds and exits. Loads `.env`/`.env.local` walking up from cwd. |
| `pylon start [app.ts] [--port N]` | Production server. Prod-shaped defaults — no auto `.pylon/`, `PYLON_DEV_MODE` defaults OFF (safe CORS/OAuth gates), expand-only schema diff. `PYLON_DEV_MODE=true` opts back into dev behavior. Requires `pylon build` first. |

Default port **4321** (`--port`/`-p`). The runtime binds a port cluster:

| Port | Role |
|---|---|
| `4321` | HTTP — API, auth, studio, frontend, plus multiplexed WS at `/api/sync/ws` |
| `4322` | dedicated WebSocket — live queries + CRDT sync |
| `4323` | dedicated SSE — change-event fallback transport |
| `4324` | shard WebSocket (only when a shard registry is configured) |

## Storage

The app model is identical on either backend — only the connection string changes.

- **SQLite (default).** DB at `.pylon/dev.db`; sessions in `<db>.sessions.db`, jobs in `<db>.jobs.db` (derived automatically).
- **Postgres.** Set `DATABASE_URL` (`postgres://` / `postgresql://`). Takes precedence over SQLite so multi-replica deploys don't fall back to per-replica SQLite. Every auth store connects to PG. Boot is fail-fast: if `DATABASE_URL` is set but unreachable, the server refuses to start.

## Served endpoints (literal route surface, port 4321)

- `GET|POST|PATCH|PUT|DELETE /api/entities/<Entity>[/<id>]` — entity CRUD (policy-checked); plus `/cursor` and `/api/batch`
- `POST /api/fn/<name>` — call a function (`/api/fn` enumerates; `/api/fn/traces` returns traces). With `Accept: text/event-stream` → streaming output.
- `POST /api/actions/<name>` — invoke an action
- `/api/query`, `/api/transact`, `/api/lookup`, `/api/aggregate`
- `/api/auth/*` — full auth surface (`session`, `me`, `magic/send`, `magic/verify`, `callback/<provider>`, org SSO, SAML, `sso/discover`, …)
- `/api/sync/{pull,push}` and `/api/sync/ws` (WS upgrade on the main port)
- `/api/files/{init,confirm}` (3-step upload: init → client PUT → confirm), `/api/files/<id>`
- `/api/{link,unlink}`, `/api/crdt/<entity>/<row>`, `/api/shards/<…>`
- `/api/rooms/{join,leave,presence,broadcast}`, `/api/rooms[/<room>]`
- `/api/cache`, `/api/pubsub/*`, `/api/jobs[/…]`, `/api/scheduler`, `/api/workflows[/…]`
- `/api/search/<entity>`, `/api/manifest`
- `/api/llm/complete`, `/api/ai/complete`, `POST /api/ai/stream` (streaming AI; auth required, rate-limited)
- `/api/admin/users/<id>/{export,purge}` (GDPR), `/admin/*`
- `/api/webhooks/<name>` (function-backed)
- `/studio*` — admin Studio UI (admin-auth required in prod)
- `GET /health`, `GET /health/deep`, `GET /metrics` (metrics needs `PYLON_ADMIN_TOKEN`/`PYLON_METRICS_TOKEN` bearer in non-dev)
- **Frontend/SSR:** non-API `GET`/`HEAD` serve the built SPA or proxy the dev server; `mode == "ssr"` manifest routes are server-rendered.

> On **Cloudflare Workers**, `/api/auth/*` returns `501 AUTH_UNAVAILABLE_ON_WORKERS` (native crypto doesn't cross-compile to wasm32). Use Fly for full auth, or bearer-token auth via custom routes on Workers.

## Environment variables (selected; all names literal)

**Mode & secrets:** `PYLON_DEV_MODE` (`1`/`true` → relaxed CORS/CSRF/OAuth gates), `PYLON_SECRET` (32-byte at-rest key for SSO/SAML secrets), `PYLON_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (32-byte hex/base64; required for `field.encrypted()` + connections), `PYLON_JWT_SECRET` + `PYLON_JWT_ISSUER` (JWT bearer auth; both required together), `PYLON_ADMIN_TOKEN`, `PYLON_METRICS_TOKEN`, `PYLON_ADMIN_EMAILS`.

**Storage:** `DATABASE_URL` (Postgres; wins over SQLite), `PYLON_SESSION_DB`, `PYLON_JOBS_DB`, `PYLON_SESSION_IN_MEMORY`, `PYLON_JOBS_IN_MEMORY`.

**CORS/CSRF/proxy:** `PYLON_CORS_ORIGIN` (comma list; prod refuses `*`, prod with none is a hard boot error), `PYLON_CSRF_ORIGINS`, `PYLON_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, `PYLON_TRUST_PROXY_HOPS`.

**Rate limiting:** `PYLON_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (anon/IP), `PYLON_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_AUTHED`, `PYLON_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW`, `PYLON_FN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`/`_WINDOW`, `PYLON_AI_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`/`_WINDOW`.

**Frontend/SSR:** `PYLON_FRONTEND_DIR`, `PYLON_FRONTEND_DEV_PROXY`.

**LLM/AI:** `PYLON_LLM_PROVIDER` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `PYLON_LLM_MODEL`, `PYLON_AI_MODELS_ALLOWED`; legacy `PYLON_AI_PROVIDER`/`PYLON_AI_API_KEY`/`PYLON_AI_MODEL`/`PYLON_AI_BASE_URL` for the `/api/ai/*` surface.

**Email:** `PYLON_EMAIL_PROVIDER` (`sendgrid`|`resend`|`stack0`|`webhook`), `PYLON_EMAIL_API_KEY`, `PYLON_EMAIL_FROM`, `PYLON_EMAIL_ENDPOINT`.

**Files:** `PYLON_FILES_PROVIDER` (`local` default | `stack0` | S3-compatible). Local: `PYLON_FILES_DIR` (default `uploads/`). Stack0: `PYLON_STACK0_API_KEY` + `PYLON_STACK0_PROJECT_SLUG`. S3: `PYLON_S3_BUCKET`/`_REGION`/`_ENDPOINT`/`_ACCESS_KEY`/`_SECRET_KEY`/`_PUBLIC_URL`.

**Cluster/cloud:** `PYLON_CLUSTER_BUS` (`redis://`; unset → single-machine), `PYLON_CLOUD_URL` (override the Pylon Cloud origin, default `https://cloud.pylonsync.com`).

> The dev/start server takes its port from `--port`/`-p` (default `4321`) or the platform's `internal_port`. Note: a `PYLON_PORT` env var exists (`config.rs`, and Pylon's generated systemd unit + `.env.example` set it), but the `pylon dev`/`pylon start` serving path does not currently read it — pass `--port` to be sure.

---

# 9. CLI reference

`pylon` — AI-native framework for web/mobile apps. `--json` is parsed globally (any command emits machine-readable JSON when present). `--help`/`-h` short-circuits. Logging via `RUST_LOG`, `PYLON_LOG_FORMAT=json|pretty` (logs to stderr).

## Local development & build

- **`pylon dev [app.ts|schema.ts] [-p N] [--once] [--json]`** — dev server with hot reload; serves SSR + API on one port; loads `.env`/`.env.local`. Auto-discovers entry (`app.ts` → `schema.ts`).
- **`pylon start [app.ts] [-p N]`** — production server, no watcher/codegen. Requires `pylon build` first.
- **`pylon build [app.ts] [--out dir] [--no-client] [--no-static] [--json]`** — compiles manifest, generates typed client, builds the SSR frontend bundle.
- **`pylon init [--frontend nextjs|react|tanstack|none] [--template t] [--bun] [--yes] [--overwrite]`** — scaffold a project.
- **`pylon cache [...]`** — standalone cache server.

## Codegen

- **`pylon codegen [app.ts|schema.ts]`** — generates BOTH `pylon.manifest.json` and `pylon.client.ts`. Flags: `--out`/`--manifest-out`, `--client-out`, `--no-client`.
- **`pylon codegen client [manifest.json] --target ts|swift [--out path]`** — regenerate just the typed client (`--out -` → stdout). This is how the Swift SDK client is generated.

## Auth (Pylon Cloud)

- **`pylon login [--code XXXX-XXXX] [--token <t>] [--token-stdin]`** — authenticate against Pylon Cloud (or `PYLON_CLOUD_URL`). Persists to `~/.config/pylon/credentials.json`. Env: `PYLON_CLI_TOKEN`.
- **`pylon logout`** — remove stored credentials.

## Deploy & link

- **`pylon deploy [manifest.json] [--target cloud|docker|fly|compose|workers|systemd|manifest] [--project slug] [--out dir]`** — no `--target` (or `cloud`) deploys to Pylon Cloud. File targets validate the manifest and write `pylon.manifest.json` + `pylon.client.ts` + static pages into `--out` (default `deploy`).
- **`pylon link [--project slug] [--repo r] [--branch b] [--root-dir d] [--yes] [--no-browser]`** — connect the project to a GitHub repo for auto-deploy.

## Cloud project management

Cloud commands resolve the active slug via `.pylon/project`, `--project <slug>`, or env, and require `pylon login`.

- **`pylon projects [list|use <slug>|current]`** — list (default), pin a slug, or show the active one.
- **`pylon secrets [list|set KEY=value|set KEY|rm KEY|import .env [--replace]]`** — manage cloud secrets.
- **`pylon logs [tail] [--limit N] [--follow] [--json]`** — stream the request log. `--limit N` is one-shot and agent-safe. `--json` emits one JSON object per line (timestamp/method/path/status/cpu_ms/bytes_out/region/error).
- **`pylon domains [list|add <host>|verify <host>|rm <host>]`**.
- **`pylon db [list|backup|restore <id>]`** — cloud DB snapshots (`restore` takes `--yes`).
- **`pylon data [entities|list <Entity>|get <Entity> <id>]`** — inspect cloud data (`list --limit N`, default 50, clamped 1–1000).
- **`pylon deployments [list|rollback <id>]`**.
- **`pylon members [list|invite <email> [role]]`**.
- **`pylon status`** — uptime, requests, jobs, realtime WS/SSE counts.
- **`pylon fn <name> [key=value ...] [--json]`** — call any cloud function (`POST /api/fn/<name>`). Value syntax: string default; `42`/`3.14` number; `true`/`false` bool; `null`; `@path.json` file body; inline JSON `{...}`/`[...]`.

## Schema & migrations

- **`pylon schema <check|diff|push|inspect|history>`** — validate / diff / push schema (`--sqlite <path>`, `--postgres <url>`, `--dry-run`), inspect live DB, or show migration history.
- **`pylon migrate <create <name>|list|status|plan|apply|auto>`** — `apply` takes `--yes`, `--allow-destructive`; `auto` implies `--yes`. Migrations dir `migrations/`, table `_pylon_migrations`.
- **`pylon seed [--file path] [--port N] [--token t]`** — seed from JSON.

## Quality & security

- **`pylon lint [--strict] [--json]`** — static manifest analysis. Rules: `PYL001` (`allow:"true"` on a tenant-shaped entity), `PYL002` (entity with zero policies), `PYL003` (`data.X==auth.userId` without matching `existing.X` on update), `PYL004` (`allowRead` only, no write rules). Plus function-level rules `PYL005`/`PYL006` (run via the TS pass, not the manifest-only analyzer). Also runs at `pylon dev` startup; `--strict` exits non-zero on warnings.
- **`pylon test [filter] [--json]`** — runs `*.test.ts` in `tests/` (or `functions/`) via `bun test` with `PYLON_IN_MEMORY=1`, `PYLON_DEV_MODE=1`.
- **`pylon test:security [--target url] [--strict] [--json]`** — adversarial anonymous probe of every manifest function/entity against a running server (default target `http://localhost:4321`).

## Other

- **`pylon backup` / `pylon restore`** — local DB backup/restore (`--yes`).
- **`pylon plugins [list|search <q>|info <name>]`**, **`pylon doctor`** (env check), **`pylon env`** (env var reference), **`pylon explain <code>`** (look up an error code, e.g. `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `FORBIDDEN`), **`pylon version`**.

---

# 10. Deploy

`pylon deploy [manifest] [--target <t>] [--out <dir>]`. No `--target` (or `--target cloud`) deploys to **Pylon Cloud**. Other targets generate IaaS config into `deploy/` (manifest + `pylon.client.ts` + static pages always written).

| `--target` | Generates |
|---|---|
| `cloud` *(default)* | Packages + deploys to Pylon Cloud (`cloud.pylonsync.com`, override `PYLON_CLOUD_URL`). Auth via `pylon login`. |
| `docker` | `Dockerfile` (Rust builder → Debian slim, `EXPOSE 4321`) |
| `fly` | `Dockerfile` + `fly.toml` |
| `compose` | `docker-compose.yml` + `Dockerfile` |
| `workers` | Cloudflare Workers `wrangler.toml` (experimental; no native auth) |
| `systemd` | systemd unit file for VPS deploys |
| `manifest` | just the manifest + client bindings + static pages |

**Fly reference** (`examples/erp/fly.toml`): HTTP `internal_port = 4321` with `force_https`; a second TCP service on `4322` (WS) with a TLS handler; a `/data` volume mount; `auto_stop_machines`. Set secrets to leave dev mode:

```sh
fly secrets set --app <app> \
  PYLON_DEV_MODE=false \
  PYLON_CORS_ORIGIN=https://your-frontend.example.com
```

The server refuses to boot in non-dev mode without a CORS origin (otherwise a silent restart loop).

---

# Appendix — the canonical authoring loop

1. **Define an entity** in `app.ts` / `apps/api/schema.ts` (`entity()` + `field.*`).
2. **Write a policy** for it (`policy({ entity, allowRead, allowInsert, ... })`) — omitted actions deny by default. Start permissive in dev, tighten for prod (`pylon lint` flags wide-open tenant entities).
3. **Author a function** in `functions/<name>.ts` (`query`/`mutation`/`action`, `default`-exported, `auth` defaults to `"user"`). Server functions bypass policies — gate on `ctx.auth` there.
4. **Read it on the client** with `db.useQuery("Entity")` (live) or `db.useQueryOne("Entity", id)`; call functions with `db.fn(...)` / `callFn(...)`; on SSR pages read via `use(serverData.list("Entity"))` inside `<Suspense>`.
5. **Run `pylon dev`** — one port, SSR + API, hot reload, typed client regenerated on every change. Use `pylon logs --json`, `pylon data`, `pylon status` to inspect; `pylon deploy` to ship.
